text: Rust allows only one mutable reference to a value at a time so mutation stays exclusive and no other reference can read or write that memory while it changes. That rule prevents data races.
thought:
Rust forbids simultaneous mutable references to the same value to prevent data races. This prevents the bug class of concurrent modification.

The borrow checker enforces that a value may have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references, but never both. Two mutable references would allow concurrent writes to the same memory, even in single-threaded code through aliasing.

Mutable aliasing also causes iterator invalidation and use-after-free bugs when one reference invalidates another's assumptions.
